item.title: Adeleke sworn in for 2nd term; says ‘Let’s heal our past wounds’
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As Governor Ademola Adeleke took oath of office for his second term tenure, he has charged the Osun State political class to allow the wounds of the past to heal and collaborate to develop the state. Governor Adeleke spoke while addressing hundreds of dignitaries and residents who thronged the Osogbo township stadium to be part of his inauguration. He disclosed that citizens, irrespective of political affiliations, must unite for the collective good. His words: “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content”. The governor commended the resilience of the citizens and residents of the state to safeguard democracy, saying their commitment has become a national model. “Today is a triumph of the people’s will. I give all glory to God and deeply thank the people of Osun. Their commitment to democracy is today a national model,” he said. 2nd term focus On his administration’s focus for the second term, he said the target of the government will focus on citizens’ welfare, infrastructure expansion, industrialisation, agricultural transformation, digital economy, tourism industry, wealth creation, and youth and women’s development among others. “As growth depends on steady power supply, we will immediately set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission. This is in line with the power sector law I signed earlier this year. “Job and Wealth creation will be at the heart of our second term. We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” Osun local government crisis On the issue of local government crisis, Adeleke said: “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter. In the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres.” Earlier, the deputy governor, Kola Adewusi took oath of office at 11:24a.m. followed by that of the governor whose oath of office was administered by the Chief Judge, Justice Oyebola Adepele-Ojo at exactly 11:34am. Vice President Shettima, Ooni, others Meanwhile, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima led dignitaries from all spheres of life to the inauguration. The National leader of the APC, Chief Bisi Akande; Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa; former National Secretary of the party, Senator Iyiola Omisore, PDP’s National Treasurer, Prince Diran Odeyemi and former Presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Datti-Baba Ahmed, were also in attendance. item.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
item.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. Ghana Ghana introduced a free visa policy for African nationals in May 2026. Under the arrangement, African travellers can apply for electronic visas without paying visa fees. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. item.title: Kano govt to Kwankwaso: Stop dragging Yusuf into EFCC troubles
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has asked former Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to stop linking Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to his alleged dealings with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The government said Yusuf had no involvement in Kwankwaso’s issues with the anti-graft agency, which it claimed predated the current administration. The Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, stated this in a statement issued on Friday. He described Kwankwaso’s allegations against the governor as misleading and politically motivated. According to the government, it was wrong for the former governor to accuse Yusuf of influencing the EFCC investigation when the matter began before his administration. “The crisis and court cases involving the NDC are internal party matters arising from disagreements among its members, and the Kano State Government has no involvement in them,” the statement said. The government accused Kwankwaso of using the governor as a target to gain public sympathy and remain politically relevant ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Rather than constantly blaming the Kano State Government for his political difficulties, Kwankwaso should concentrate on resolving the internal challenges confronting his political camp,” the statement said. It maintained that Yusuf was elected to govern Kano State and deliver development, not to engage in political arguments or take responsibility for the problems of other political parties. The government urged Kwankwaso to allow the administration to focus on fulfilling its promises to the people, warning that attempts to gain public sympathy through political blackmail would not succeed. “You cannot win public sympathy through blackmail and unfounded allegations,” it said. The statement added that the people of Kano State would have the opportunity to judge political leaders through their votes in 2027. It further reaffirmed that Yusuf remained committed to governance, development and the welfare of residents. Recall that Kwankwaso had accused Governor Yusuf of using the EFCC and other government institutions to target him and members of his family for political reasons ahead of the 2027 elections. He also alleged that the governor attempted to pressure the EFCC through protests at its office and interfere in a case involving the NDC governorship candidate. item.title: Obasanjo unhappy Tinubu is delivering on promises — FHA director
item.description: B y Dapo Akinrefon An Executive Director (Projects Implementation) of the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Oluremi Omowaiye, has criticised former President Olusegun Obasanjo over his remarks on President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, alleging that the former president was uncomfortable with the achievements of the current administration. Omowaiye, who defended Tinubu’s economic policies, said Obasanjo was unhappy because the President had achieved what he failed to accomplish during his eight years in office. Obasanjo had criticised the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, arguing that they had pushed many Nigerians deeper into poverty. However, reacting to the former president’s position in a statement on Friday, Omowaiye, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said Obasanjo should be ashamed of his comments, insisting that Tinubu had surpassed his achievements. “Obasanjo should cover his face in shame. He is unhappy because we have Yoruba man who has done what he failed to do as president. He is uncomfortable because President Tinubu has surpassed his achievements,” he said. The FHA director further alleged that Obasanjo was uncomfortable with Tinubu’s performance because the President was delivering on his promises and could secure another four-year term in 2027. “Obasanjo is unhappy because President Tinubu is delivering on his promises and he knows he is going to achieve much more when he gets reelected for another four years. That is why he is doing everything to stop it but he won’t succeed. “Nigerians are happy with the President’s Renewed Hope agenda and they want him to continue,” Omowaiye said. Questioning Obasanjo’s claim that Tinubu’s reforms had made Nigerians 300 per cent poorer, Omowaiye argued that the former president’s business interests continued to operate despite the economic difficulties he had highlighted. He specifically cited Bells University and Obasanjo Farms, asking whether the former president had shut down either business because of the financial challenges facing Nigerians. “Did he close down Bells University because students are unable to pay? No. Has he closed down Obasanjo Farms because the economy is so bad?” he asked. Omowaiye also cited Next Cash and Carry supermarket, which he described as Nigeria’s biggest single supermarket, arguing that its continued operation after a fire incident demonstrated that businesses could still thrive despite economic challenges. “Peter Obi that Obasanjo is supporting has the biggest single supermarket in Nigeria. It got burnt sometimes ago. He rebuilt it and it is doing fine today. If the economy is so bad, will Next Supermarket be doing fine?” he queried. He also faulted Obasanjo over the state of infrastructure during his presidency, particularly the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which he described as the country’s most economically viable road. item.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Tyson suffered the first two defeats of his professional career against Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, leaving him with 39 professional fights on his record. The post Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim

item.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
item.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. item.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
item.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. item.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
item.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. item.title: Tyson Fury’s Wife Backtracks On Schizophrenia Claim
item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, has retracted her claim that the British heavyweight was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after he was crowned world champion in 2015. In clips promoting a Netflix documentary, the boxer spoke about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in Germany. Paris Fury said Tyson Fury had “mild schizophrenia” in an initial version of the documentary, which will be released on Friday. Netflix said it had worked to “update” the footage in light of her clarification. Fury, 38, is due to face Anthony Joshua in a long-awaited all-British showdown in Cardiff on December 11. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. “I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a break of nearly three years from boxing. item.title: Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen
item.description: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in western Yemen, Houthi media said, a day after an attack by the Iran-backed movement on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the armed group since the country’s civil war reignited over the summer. In response, Houthi forces have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and the financial district of the capital, Riyadh. Saudi warplanes carried out a raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Taiz governorate on Friday, killing “11 citizens, most of them children,” the Houthis’ Saba news agency said, citing a local source. The agency also reported strikes targeting fuel tanks in the Saada region, the movement’s birthplace and stronghold. Smoke billows from the Yemeni capital Sanaa on November 26, 2026 after Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territories held by the Iran-backed group, hours after it struck Riyadh. Photo by AFP On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The attack also triggered a fire that led to the shutdown of the facility, the SPA said. Yemen plunged back into war in July, after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the Middle East war. Hostilities intensified in September when the Houthis, who already controlled the most densely populated parts of Yemen, seized the western coastline overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait on the Red Sea. The Houthis are now advancing toward Aden, a major southern city where the government has taken refuge after being driven out of the capital Sanaa in 2015. Since the conflict resumed, fighting in Yemen has killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over 364,000, according to the United Nations. In Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks have killed 27 people, according to the kingdom’s authorities. The post Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: UN warns of worsening hunger in northern Nigeria, 15 other areas
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The United Nations has warned of worsening hunger across 16 regions of the world over the next six months, identifying northern Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Yemen as areas facing the highest risk of acute food insecurity. The warning was contained in a joint report by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), which attributed the growing food crisis to armed conflicts, climate extremes, economic shocks and declining humanitarian assistance. The report, released on Friday, covers the period from December 2026 to May 2027 and cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further in several African countries as conflict and extreme weather events continue to disrupt livelihoods and food production. It identified Sudan and South Sudan as countries where famine remains a plausible risk, particularly in parts of North Darfur. The agencies also expressed concern over rising political violence, noting that incidents had increased by more than 15 per cent compared with the same period last year. The development, according to the report, has triggered significant displacement in recent months, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen, further worsening the humanitarian situation. It also highlighted a sharp decline in humanitarian funding to the five countries facing the highest levels of concern. According to the agencies, humanitarian assistance to the countries fell by nearly two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, dropping from $5.1bn to $2bn. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” the report stated. The agencies warned that previous humanitarian interventions had helped prevent famine in affected areas, but the improvements were often temporary, with severe food insecurity returning within a few years. Other areas classified as facing very high concern include Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Palestine and Haiti. The report noted that gang violence in Haiti had displaced about 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access, while the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to grapple with an Ebola outbreak. Chad, Uganda, Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor were also added to the list of hunger hotspots. The agencies warned that the impact of El Niño could worsen food production in several of these regions, particularly through irregular rainfall, drought and flooding. item.title: Powerful Storm Disrupts US Thanksgiving, Leaves Over 900,000 Without Power
item.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. Stay Safe People brave the bad weather in the Manhattan borough of New York City on November 26, 2026. Photo by KENA BETANCUR / AFP While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. “Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X. Some people improvised to still enjoy Thanksgiving, which is traditionally marked by gathering with family around a large meal, with turkey as the centerpiece. “No electricity? No problem,” celebrity chef Jose Andres wrote on X, alongside a video of a candlelit dining room and lobsters cooking on a gas-powered stove. item.title: Conflicts, El Nino Worsening Hunger — UN
item.description: UN food agencies warned Friday of worsening hunger over the next six months in 16 mostly African areas, with ongoing conflicts exacerbating already dire conditions in countries like Sudan and Yemen. While armed conflict and violence are the main reasons for acute food insecurity around the globe, dramatic climate events, including El Nino, are another driver, the joint report from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) said. The Rome-based agencies listed Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen as the areas of highest concern in its early warning about 16 “hunger hotspots” from December until May 2027. Famine remains a “plausible” risk in parts of Sudan — including North Darfur — and South Sudan, the report found. ‘Alarming levels of displacement’ The indoor cooking setup of a local food vendor, featuring large metal pots resting on industrial gas stoves. The stoves are connected directly to an orange gas cylinder running on the clean, smoke-free biogas produced by the biodigester. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) The risk of worsening hunger comes amid a rise in “political violence events” around the world, up by more than 15 percent over the same period a year earlier, which has prompted “alarming levels of displacement in recent months”, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen. In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1 billion to $2 billion. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote FAO and WFP. While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks — including risk of famine — re-emerged within a few years.” Also classified as a “very high concern” are Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo — which is also struggling to contend with an outbreak of Ebola — Palestine, and Haiti, where expanding gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access. New additions to the list are Chad, Uganda, the Southern Africa region and the Central American Dry Corridor, a tropical dry forest extending from Guatemala to Costa Rica, with the latter two regions expected to be hit by the effects of El Nino, adversely affecting crops. The list also includes Mali, Myanmar and Madagascar. “Targeted humanitarian action is urgently needed to save lives and livelihoods across all hunger hotspots,” read the report. “In hotspots of highest concern, such action is critical to prevent starvation and loss of life.” Too much or little rain El Nino — the ocean warming phenomenon that is disrupting weather patterns globally, provoking devastating droughts or in

item.title: 2027: Lokpobiri rallies Bayelsa West for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, has urged voters in Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Lokpobiri made the appeal on Thursday, November 26, during a pre-campaign sensitisation exercise organised by the Bayelsa West APC Campaign Directorate in Aleibiri, Ebedebiri and Agbere communities. Addressing party members, stakeholders and residents, the minister urged them to remain committed to the APC, saying sustained support for the party was necessary to consolidate the reforms and transformation being pursued by the Tinubu administration under its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said Tinubu had demonstrated the courage, vision and determination to reposition the country through what he described as bold reforms and purposeful leadership. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has remained committed to delivering on his Renewed Hope mandate and transforming our dear nation. The progress being made requires our collective support and commitment to ensure that the gains are sustained. We must therefore give him another mandate in 2027,” he said. The minister also called on the people to support all APC candidates, stressing that political unity, grassroots mobilisation and collective participation would be crucial to the party’s prospects in the elections. “I urge the good people of Bayelsa West to stand firmly with President Tinubu and all APC candidates. This is the time to consolidate our structures, strengthen our grassroots engagement and work together towards victory,” he added. The sensitisation exercise, according to the organisers, was part of the party’s efforts to strengthen grassroots mobilisation, encourage peaceful political participation and build support structures across Bayelsa West ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso accuses Kano governor of plot to tarnish his image
item.description: Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has accused Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, of allegedly orchestrating a campaign to tarnish his reputation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso made the allegation in a statement issued on Friday, expressing concern over what he described as the alleged use of anti-corruption institutions, particularly the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), for political purposes. The former Kano State governor questioned the motives behind what he characterised as attempts to damage his public image, alleging that the anti-corruption agency was being drawn into political activities. He expressed concern that institutions established to fight corruption could be used to settle political scores, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. However, the allegations against Governor Yusuf remain claims by Kwankwaso and would require an independent response from the governor or his representatives. item.title: 2027 Election:​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‌‌​‍‍‌​ INEC procures 57,000 new BVAS devices
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission has procured 57,000 new BVAS for the 2027 general elections. Prof. Amupitan disclosed this on Thursday during a sensitisation seminar by the Diocese of Abuja, Anglican Communion, on Civil and Political Education with the theme “Why Your Vote Still Matters” Represented by the Deputy Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Wilfred Ifogah, Prof. Amupitan said that the commission had also reduced the threshold from 1,250 to 850 voters per machine and cleaned the register through biometric audit. He said that with 51 days to the Jan. 16, 2027, presidential and National Assembly elections, civic responsibility must not be outsourced. Amupitan said INEC would on Saturday conduct a nationwide mock accreditation exercise in two polling units per ward to test upgrades ahead of 2027. According to him, over 10.77 million new registrants were recorded during the Continuous Voter Registration, while over 1.6 million invalid records were removed, bringing the verified register to over 100 million voters, including 232,658 persons with disabilities. He said INEC had also upgraded its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, with automated checks for over-voting and arithmetic consistency on Form EC8A before transmission. The INEC boss urged citizens to resist vote buying, divisive politics and inflammatory language, noting that Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026 prescribe stiff penalties for electoral violence and hate speech. Also speaking, a legal practitioner, Mr Emeka Etiaba, SAN, said over-judicialisation of elections was eroding public confidence. Etiaba said trust is earned, not commanded, stressing that INEC and the judiciary must deliver credible processes in 2027 to restore confidence. He noted that technicalities, poor petition drafting and non-justiciable innovations often deny determination of cases on merit, leaving a few judges to decide outcomes involving thousands of voters. He said innovations such as AI validation on IReV, though laudable administratively, must be backed by law to be enforceable in court. Speaking at the event, the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Most Rev. Henry Ndukuba, urged Nigerians, especially youths, to actively participate in the 2027 general elections. According to him, their votes remain critical to deepening democracy and national development. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the seminar is part of activities marking the 37th anniversary of the diocese and Carnival for Christ 2026. Ndukuba said the church organised the seminar to sensitise citizens on their civic responsibility ahead of the polls, and the 2027 electioneering campaigns were already underway, with general elections scheduled for January 2027.
